cohort: The study included 14,624 women having singleton births, categorized by their BMI during pregnancy.
finding: Women with increasing BMI had increasingly higher odds of adverse outcomes such as GDM, GHT, CD, and PPH, while underweight women were associated with increased odds of PTB, LBW, and congenital anomalies.
mod_finding: Increasing maternal BMI was associated with increasingly higher odds of cesarean delivery, with the highest odds observed in the class III obesity group (aOR 2.33).
